definition: The twilight; that brief, luminous interval between sunset and full dark when the sky holds its last warmth of color and the world seems briefly suspended between two states.
etymology: From Old English glom, meaning twilight or dusk, itself from a Proto-Germanic root related to gleam — as if the fading sky were still trying, quietly, to glow. The Scots carried the word forward with particular affection, giving us gloaming in the form we still use today.
usage: On the longest evenings of the year, the gloaming stretches itself out luxuriously, refusing to hurry toward night — and June 18th, so close to the solstice, offers as generous a gloaming as the calendar allows.
